Disabling interrupts here keeps cpuid/mycpu results valid, so a thread doesn't migrate to another CPU. It doesn't address protecting shared data from other CPUs.

grades.quote: Interrupts may still occur on other CPUs, so an interrupt’s acquire can wait for a thread to release a spinlock; just not on the same CPU.
grades.reason: It states that disabling interrupts is per-CPU. Interrupts and code on other CPUs still run, so a spinlock is still needed to make them wait. It never states outright that interrupt disabling alone fails to protect shared data, so it only partly answers the question.
